summary: Buchanan Lookout above Kaslo: first lookout built 1920, cab replaced 1965, retired from fire detection, restored by 2014 and kept as a recreation site.

facts.design: 4.3 m by 4.3 m (14 ft by 14 ft) cab with catwalk on a 5.5 m (18 ft) concrete block tower

staffing.status: no longer used for fire detection

access.note: Recreation site, road and outside catwalk open; interior closed per 2014 provincial release. 1998 register entry said open to the public in summer months; a travel site says locked.

visit.trail_note: Buchanan Viewpoint Trail (2 km), wheelchair-accessible toilet, two small campsites. Interior closed; windows viewable from the outside catwalk.

events.note: Present cab and 18 ft concrete block tower replaced the first lookout.
Start of operation as a fire lookout, per a 2022 trip report (single source).
End of operation as a fire lookout, per a 2022 trip report (single source).
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, August 15, 1998.
Province announced substantial exterior and interior restoration complete, structure rebuilt to current safety standards.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1998 register entry says open to the public in summer months; the 2014 provincial release says the interior is closed and viewable only through catwalk windows; a travel site says locked. The story follows the 2014 release, the most recent official account.

The province gives 1,912 m, the recreation page 1,908 m, and a travel site about 1,945 m. The brief's 1908.7 m is close to the recreation page. The story gives the province's figure and reports the others.
A recreation page says 2WD is suitable, a 2022 trip report says a 4x4 with clearance is fine, and a travel site recommends high clearance. The story reports all three without choosing one.

notes_for_editor: Operating years 1941 to 1982 come from one 2022 hiking trip report only; the NHLR says just 'no longer used'. The 18 ft figure is the concrete tower alone, so height_m is omitted rather than guessed. Access and road accounts conflict across sources. The 2014 release describes a partnership to maintain the site, and no later source was read. A 2012 centennial restoration is mentioned in a BC Forest Service brochure that was not read. Other unread leads: canada-lookouts.weebly.com (1965/1982/2012 dates) and ithinkwemissedaturn.com (1986 rec site).
